title: Continuity Check: Does the Limit Match the Value?
caption_md: Drag the epsilon slider toward 0 and watch the two approach dots squeeze toward $x = 2$. The limit of $f(x) = \frac{x^2 - 4}{x - 2}$ as $x \to 2$ is $4$, but the function is defined as $f(2) = 10$ (the filled dot). Because $\lim_{x \to 2} f(x) = 4 \neq 10 = f(2)$, condition 3 of continuity fails. Notice the open hole at $(2, 4)$ and the misplaced filled dot at $(2, 10)$ — that gap is exactly what discontinuity looks like.
